newsitem.title: USA: US lawmakers make offer to help TV rating talks.
newsitem.headline: US lawmakers make offer to help TV rating talks.

text.p: A group of lawmakers said Tuesday they had given assurances to the television industry aimed at helping the development of a new program ratings system.

A bipartisan letter sent Monday pledged to support a "cease fire" on program content legislation if the industry and parents groups reached agreement on adding content indicators to the age-based ratings system.

The letter to the National Cable Television Association, National Association of Broadcasters and Motion Picture Association was issued by Massachusetts Democrat Edward Markey, Indiana Republican Dan Burton, Virginia Democrat Jim Moran, and John Spratt, a Democrat from South Carolina.
The industry continues to meet with parent groups on revamping the ratings system to include indications of whether a program contains sexual content, violence or coarse language.

"We are continuing to meet with advocacy groups and members of Congress on this issue and we're hopeful we can reach a resolution in a manner that is helpful to American parents," said Dennis Wharton, spokesman for the broadcasters.
